title: Python bytecode (.pyc) signature
summary: A Python 3.7+ bytecode file (.pyc) begins with a 16-byte header: a 4-byte magic number (version-specific, e.g. 0xCB0D0DF3 for 3.11), a 4-byte null (flags), a 4-byte modification timestamp (or 0 for hash-based), and a 4-byte source file size (or hash).
source_version: Wikipedia List of file signatures, retrieved 2026-05-29

notes: Magic number varies by Python version (e.g. 0xCB0D0DF3 for 3.11, 0xA70D0DF3 for 3.10, 0x610D0DF3 for 3.9).
Bytes 8-11: mtime (timestamp-based) or first 4 bytes of the source hash.
Bytes 12-15: source size (timestamp-based) or remaining hash bytes.
The marshal module serializes the code object after the header.
